posts.title: Xiaomi unveils 3-nm Xring D100 smart-driving chip, plans commercial use in 2027
posts.summary:
Xiaomi said the Xring D100 is China's first high-computing-power smart-driving chip built on a 3-nm process and can run models with up to 200 billion parameters locally.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi unveiled the Xring D100, China's first 3-nm high-computing-power smart-driving chip, capable of running large language models with up to 200 billion parameters locally.
The chip features a 20-core CPU and 16-core NPU, with commercial deployment scheduled for 2027 as Xiaomi seeks to reduce reliance on external suppliers like Nvidia.
Xiaomi has invested over 21 billion yuan in its semiconductor program, which now employs nearly 3,000 experts to drive hardware-software integration.
The D100 launch intensifies the competitive landscape among Chinese EV makers, joining peers like Nio and Li Auto in the race to develop proprietary, high-performance silicon.

posts.title: Leapmotor stays profitable in H1 as margin and cash flow weaken
posts.summary:
Leapmotor's first-half net profit rose to 210 million yuan ($30.95 million), marking its second consecutive half-year of profitability.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Leapmotor achieved its second consecutive half-year of profitability with a net profit of 210 million yuan, representing a 600% year-on-year increase.
Despite revenue growth of 57.2% to 38.11 billion yuan, the company's gross margin narrowed to 11.7% due to rising raw material costs and product mix shifts.
Free cash flow plummeted 83.7% to 140 million yuan, reflecting heavy investment in inventory, R&D, and sales expansion.
Overseas expansion is a critical growth pillar, with exports surging 372.6% to 96,294 vehicles, now accounting for 27% of total sales.

posts.title: Multi-Die Assemblies Dominate At 2nm And Below
posts.summary:
Chips are getting bigger, more modular, and much more capable as new innovations mix with existing processes and long-researched projects go mainstream.
The post Multi-Die Assemblies Dominate At 2nm And Below appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Heterogeneous integration and multi-die assemblies have become essential for leading-edge servers and edge devices as traditional monolithic scaling hits physical and economic limits.
The shift is driven by the inability to meet AI performance demands through transistor shrinking alone, necessitating the use of chiplets to overcome reticle-size constraints.
The rise of agentic AI is increasing architectural complexity by requiring a mix of CPUs, GPUs, and specialized accelerators, which complicates the validation and manufacturability of new designs.

Industry leaders are targeting a two-order-of-magnitude improvement in performance-per-watt, a goal that requires a fundamental realignment of manufacturing processes and advanced packaging technologies.

bullets: A significant political backlash against AI data centers is emerging ahead of the US midterms, with bipartisan opposition growing due to environmental and infrastructure concerns.
New reports suggest that a proposed Amazon data center could become the most polluting power plant in the United States, highlighting the tension between AI growth and energy policy.
The luxury travel sector is expanding into the 'space economy,' with firms like SpaceVIP facilitating private missions to the International Space Station at costs reaching $50 million per passenger.

posts.title: Kids outlearn AI—and we still don’t know why
posts.summary: People have been talking to each other for at least 100,000 years, as best we can tell. And in all that time, there has been only one thing in the world that could learn a human language to perfect fluency: a human child.  Now there are two.  Four short years after the release of ChatGPT,…
bullets: Current LLMs require approximately 100,000 times more linguistic data than a human child to achieve fluency, a disparity known as the 'data efficiency gap.'
While frontier models like Llama 3.1 utilize up to 15 trillion tokens for pretraining, experts warn that the supply of high-quality, easily accessible internet data could be exhausted by the 2030s.
Cognitive scientists are studying how children master language with minimal input to inform the development of more sustainable, data-efficient AI architectures.
The reliance on scaling model size and data volume is facing diminishing returns, shifting the focus of AI research toward biological learning mechanisms to overcome future data scarcity.
